extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and scholars of literature and postcolonial studies
extracted.subtask_short: literary criticism of Heart of Darkness
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries and debates about Chinua Achebe's 1975 essay 'An Image of Africa' critiquing Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness; presents criteria, counterarguments, and scholarly responses used to evaluate Conrad's representation of Africa and Africans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bestow human expression on Africans
rubrics_metrics.description: Conrad refuses to bestow "human expression" on Africans, even depriving them of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achebe argues that a key criterion for humane representation is granting characters human expression and language; failing to do so dehumanizes the subject and is a central charge of racism in narrative depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid depicting Africa as 'the other world' / antithesis of Europe
rubrics_metrics.description: Africa is rendered as "a foil to Europe, as a place of negations at once remote and vaguely familiar," i.e. "'the other world', the antithesis of Europe and therefore of civilization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a text frames a geographic/cultural space primarily as the negative or antithetical counterpart to the author's own culture; Achebe attributes such framing to a "residue of antipathy to black people."

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid demeaning language and fixation on racialized terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of racial slurs and obsessive references to 'blackness' (e.g., Conrad's quoted passage about a "buck nigger") indicates a problem in representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author's language includes demeaning epithets or a recurrent fixation that reduces subjects to racialized stereotypes; Achebe suggests such fixation merits psychoanalytic and ethical concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not perpetuate damaging stereotypes through canonical endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: A work included in the literary canon can continue to perpetuate damaging stereotypes of black peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the broader institutional effects of canonization: whether teaching and anthologizing a text reproduces harmful images, and whether critical framing (e.g., pairing with Achebe's critique) mitigates or exposes those harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish artistic merit from ideological content
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that Achebe's essay is "a political statement rather than a literary criticism" highlights the need to separate (or balance) judgments of artistic beauty from judgments about ideological harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a text, weigh its prose/technique and its political or ethical implications separately; defenders argue one can acknowledge "good sentences" while still critiquing representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider historical/contextual factors in judging representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defenders often cite the historical context of the author as a reason to temper charges of racism or to explain depictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether context (time, prevailing attitudes, author's biography) explains, mitigates, or fails to excuse problematic representations; this is used as a counter-criterion in debates about Conrad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the work function as anti-imperialist critique?
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics (e.g., Cedric Watts, Edward Said) defend Heart of Darkness as an anti-imperialist novel that criticizes racial prejudice and empire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative critiques imperialism and racial prejudice—if so, this may complicate claims that the work straightforwardly endorses racist views; examine textual evidence of anti-imperialist stance and its limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants agency and freedom to colonized characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a text criticizes imperialism, it may fail to "grant the natives their freedom"—i.e., depict colonized peoples as full agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether characters from colonized groups are portrayed with autonomy, voice, and subjectivity, rather than being rendered passive, voiceless, or merely symbolic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine mimetic continuities across opposing representations
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be an "underlying mimetic continuity" between colonial images of Africa (Conrad) and postcolonial representations (Achebe's Things Fall Apart) despite apparent opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically investigate structural or representational similarities that persist beneath overtly oppositional readings; look for patterns of depiction that reproduce similar tropes even when framed differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: A good critical reading should stand alongside other readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Achebe insists his reading should "stand beside these other readings" rather than demand suppression of alternate interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuate criticism partly by its engagement with plural readings: a rigorous critique acknowledges existing interpretations and argues why it should be considered alongside them, rather than attempting to nullify other perspectives.
